name: RailYatra
tagline: Train ticketing where the busiest minute of the day is 10:00 AM
summary: RailYatra books train tickets for 12 lakh passengers a day: search, booking, berth allocation, payments, PNR status, cancellations and SMS. Every morning at 10:00 the Tatkal window opens and a busy site becomes one of the busiest in the country. Double-booked berths, 'money debited, no ticket' and late OTPs keep coming back.

tour.headline: Berths are allotted without a row lock, so every Tatkal rush can double-book a seat; fixing it costs 20 hours.

incidents.title: My Bookings page takes 40 seconds to load
incidents.desc: Passengers opening My Bookings waited up to 40 seconds; the page searched every PNR for the passenger's mobile number.
whys: My Bookings was very slow
Each load searched all PNRs for the passenger's mobile number
My Bookings looks up PNRs with a full table scan by mobile number
incidents.fix: Limited the page to the last 90 days of bookings.
incidents.lesson: Limiting the window hides the missing index.

incidents.title: Booking site down for 14 minutes when Tatkal opened
incidents.desc: At 10:00 the AC Tatkal window opened and the site returned 503 errors until 10:14; about 1.8 lakh passengers could not book.
whys: The site returned 503 errors from 10:00 to 10:14
Booking servers ran out of worker threads within seconds
Every Tatkal request hits the booking servers at once with no admission queue
incidents.fix: Added 20 more booking servers for the Tatkal hour.
incidents.lesson: More servers move the cliff; they do not remove it.

incidents.title: Same berth allotted to two passengers on the Rajdhani
incidents.desc: Two passengers with confirmed Tatkal tickets were given berth B2-34 on the same journey; the TTE had to move one of them.
whys: Two confirmed tickets had the same berth
Two bookings allocated the berth at the same moment
Berth allocation reads and writes seats without a row-level lock
incidents.fix: Added a uniqueness check when the chart is prepared.
incidents.lesson: A check at chart time finds the clash hours too late.

incidents.title: Login OTPs arriving 6 minutes late before Tatkal
incidents.desc: Between 09:50 and 10:05 OTP SMS took up to 6 minutes to arrive, and most affected passengers missed the Tatkal window.
whys: Passengers did not get their OTPs in time
OTP messages waited behind a bulk SMS campaign
OTP SMS share one queue with bulk promotional messages
incidents.lesson: Someone will schedule a bulk SMS at 9:45 again.

incidents.title: Money debited but no ticket for 2,100 passengers
incidents.desc: UPI and card payments were debited but the bookings were marked failed; refunds took 5 to 7 days and support was flooded.
whys: Passengers were charged without a ticket
The booking was marked failed when the bank confirmation arrived after the session expired
There is no reconciliation of bank debits against bookings
incidents.fix: Refunded the affected passengers from a manual report.
incidents.lesson: We only find these when passengers complain.

incidents.title: Seat availability enquiry times out at 09:59
incidents.desc: In the minute before Tatkal opens, availability checks take over 30 seconds and many fail, so passengers refresh again and again.
whys: Availability checks failed just before Tatkal
Each refresh ran a fresh availability query on the reservation database
Every availability enquiry queries the reservation database directly
incidents.fix: Asked passengers on social media not to refresh.
incidents.lesson: Refreshing is what people do; the system has to expect it.

incidents.title: Sleeper Tatkal opened at 10:00 after the timing change
incidents.desc: After the circular moving non-AC Tatkal to 11:00, sleeper-class Tatkal still opened at 10:00 for two days.
whys: Sleeper Tatkal opened an hour early
The new timing was changed in one place but not in the booking checks
Tatkal quota and timing rules are hard-coded in the booking code
incidents.fix: Patched the hour in two files.
incidents.lesson: Rules that change by circular should not live in code.

incidents.title: Passengers charged twice for one ticket
incidents.desc: A retry after a slow bank response created a second debit for 340 bookings; each one was refunded by hand.
whys: Passengers were debited twice
The app retried the payment and the bank processed both requests
Bank callbacks are processed without an idempotency key
incidents.lesson: Any retry can double-charge until requests carry a key.

incidents.title: Cancellation refunds stuck in 'processing' for 3 days
incidents.desc: Refund requests stayed in processing because calls to one bank hung and blocked the refund worker.
whys: Refunds did not complete
The refund worker waited forever on one bank's API
Calls to the bank payment gateway have no timeout
incidents.lesson: One slow bank stops all refunds.

incidents.title: PNR history API timing out for frequent travellers
incidents.desc: Passengers with many past journeys see 'request timed out' on My Bookings; the query reads every PNR row.
whys: My Bookings failed for frequent travellers
The query reads every PNR row to find the passenger's bookings
My Bookings looks up PNRs with a full table scan by mobile number
incidents.fix: Raised the API time limit to 60 seconds.
incidents.lesson: A longer limit is a slower failure.

incidents.title: Two Tatkal passengers allotted the same lower berth
incidents.desc: Berth S5-1 on the Karnataka Express was allotted to two passengers who booked within the same second.
whys: Two passengers got the same berth
Both bookings saw the berth as free at the same time
Berth allocation reads and writes seats without a row-level lock
incidents.fix: Moved one passenger when the chart was prepared.

incidents.title: Debited, no ticket: 900 failed bookings on Diwali Tatkal
incidents.desc: Bank confirmations arrived after the bookings had expired, so 900 passengers were charged without tickets.
whys: Passengers were charged without tickets
Late bank confirmations were ignored after the booking expired
There is no reconciliation of bank debits against bookings
incidents.fix: Ran the manual refund report again.

incidents.title: Booking servers hung at 10:02 waiting on one bank
incidents.desc: Every booking thread was waiting for one bank's payment page, so new bookings could not start for 9 minutes.
whys: Booking stopped accepting new requests
Every booking thread was blocked on calls to the slow bank
Calls to the bank payment gateway have no timeout
incidents.fix: Removed the slow bank from the payment page.
incidents.lesson: A slow dependency is worse than a dead one.

incidents.title: 503 errors for 9 minutes at the 10 AM Tatkal opening
incidents.desc: Despite the extra servers the site returned 'Service unavailable' from 10:00 to 10:09 as 2.5 lakh passengers pressed Book together.
whys: The site returned 503 errors at 10:00
Booking servers were saturated by simultaneous requests
Every Tatkal request hits the booking servers at once with no admission queue
incidents.lesson: The peak grows faster than our server count.

incidents.title: OTP SMS delayed 4 minutes at 09:55
incidents.desc: Passengers logging in for Tatkal got their OTPs after 4 minutes while a festival-offer SMS blast was running.
whys: OTPs arrived late
OTP messages queued behind the festival SMS blast
OTP SMS share one queue with bulk promotional messages
incidents.lesson: It happened again because the queue is still shared.

incidents.title: Double debit after a UPI retry
incidents.desc: UPI collect requests retried after a slow response were debited twice for 180 tickets.
whys: Passengers paid twice
The retried UPI request was treated as a new payment
Bank callbacks are processed without an idempotency key

incidents.title: Charged but booking failed for 600 Tatkal passengers
incidents.desc: Payments succeeded at the bank but the bookings show failed; refunds have not been started yet.
whys: Passengers were charged without tickets
Bank confirmations arrived after the booking sessions expired
There is no reconciliation of bank debits against bookings

incidents.title: UPI payment page spins forever when a bank is slow
incidents.desc: When one bank's UPI service slowed down, the payment page waited indefinitely and Tatkal passengers lost their seats.
whys: The payment page never completed
The call to the bank's UPI service never returned
Calls to the bank payment gateway have no timeout
incidents.fix: Moved traffic away from the slow bank by hand.
incidents.lesson: A manual switch takes 20 minutes we do not have at 10 AM.

incidents.title: Duplicate berth allocation on the Shatabdi
incidents.desc: Seat C3-45 was allotted twice in this morning's Tatkal rush; both passengers hold confirmed e-tickets.
whys: Two confirmed tickets share a seat
Concurrent bookings allocated the same seat
Berth allocation reads and writes seats without a row-level lock

incidents.title: OTP not delivered for 5 minutes before Tatkal
incidents.desc: Passengers report OTPs arriving after 10:00 while a bulk SMS campaign was running.
whys: Login OTPs were late
The OTP queue was full of promotional messages
OTP SMS share one queue with bulk promotional messages

debts.title: Allocate berths with row-level locks and a version check
debts.desc: Lock the berth row being allotted and reject the write if its version changed, so concurrent Tatkal bookings cannot take the same berth.
debts.cause: Berth allocation reads and writes seats without a row-level lock

debts.title: Virtual waiting room: a durable queue for the Tatkal window
debts.desc: Admit passengers to booking at the rate the servers can take and hold the rest in a durable queue that shows their place, instead of every request hitting booking at 10:00.
debts.cause: Every Tatkal request hits the booking servers at once with no admission queue

debts.title: Serve seat availability from a precomputed cache
debts.desc: Precompute availability per train and class every few seconds and serve cached results, so refreshes before Tatkal do not query the reservation database.
debts.cause: Every availability enquiry queries the reservation database directly

debts.title: Put a timeout on every bank gateway call
debts.desc: Give every call to a bank or UPI service a connect and read timeout so a slow bank fails fast and frees the thread.
debts.cause: Calls to the bank payment gateway have no timeout

debts.title: Idempotency keys on payment requests and bank callbacks
debts.desc: Send a unique key with every payment request and ignore repeated callbacks for the same key, so a retry can never debit twice.
debts.cause: Bank callbacks are processed without an idempotency key

debts.title: Reconcile bank debits against bookings every 15 minutes
debts.desc: A reconciliation job matches every debit with a booking; an unmatched debit is booked if seats remain, or refunded automatically.
debts.cause: There is no reconciliation of bank debits against bookings

debts.title: Separate priority queue for OTP SMS
debts.desc: Send OTP messages through their own durable queue ahead of bulk and promotional SMS, and alert when OTP delivery takes over 20 seconds.
debts.cause: OTP SMS share one queue with bulk promotional messages

debts.title: Throttle logins and rate-limit bots before the Tatkal window
debts.desc: Per-IP and per-account rate limits on login and booking, with a CAPTCHA only when a limit is crossed, so scripted bots cannot use up booking capacity.

debts.title: Serve PNR status from a read replica with a lag check
debts.desc: Route PNR status and booking-history reads to a read replica, falling back to the primary when replica lag is over 5 seconds.

debts.title: Index PNR lookups by passenger mobile number
debts.desc: Add a composite index on (mobile, journey date) so My Bookings reads only the passenger's own PNRs.
debts.cause: My Bookings looks up PNRs with a full table scan by mobile number

debts.title: Process refunds from a durable queue with retries
debts.desc: Each refund becomes a message in a durable queue with retries and a dead-letter list, so one hung bank cannot stop every refund.

debts.title: Load test the Tatkal window at 25x before each holiday season
debts.desc: A repeatable load test that replays a Tatkal opening at 25 times a normal peak against staging, run before Diwali, Chhath and summer holidays.

debts.title: Move Tatkal quota and timing rules into configuration
debts.desc: Quota sizes and opening hours per class become configuration with an effective date, changed without a code release.
debts.cause: Tatkal quota and timing rules are hard-coded in the booking code

debts.title: Idempotent booking confirmation SMS
debts.desc: Send one confirmation SMS per PNR even when the booking event is delivered twice.

spike.name: Tatkal opening at 10 AM
spike.description: AC Tatkal opens at 10:00 and non-AC at 11:00: lakhs of passengers log in from 09:45 and press Book in the same second, twenty-five times a normal peak.
